evals.prompt: Where do I go to use the Microsoft Teams Admin Center?
evals.expected_output: Returns Microsoft Teams Admin Center with https://admin.teams.microsoft.com, includes https://aka.ms/teamsadmincenter as a secondary URL, references the source-backed portal entry, and does not invent URLs.
assertions: The output includes Microsoft Teams Admin Center
The output includes https://admin.teams.microsoft.com
The output includes https://aka.ms/teamsadmincenter
The output references msportals admin.json or Teams source references

evals.prompt: Help me figure out why a user has a different Teams meeting policy than expected before we change anything.
evals.expected_output: Uses Microsoft Learn MCP or official Microsoft documentation, starts with read-only policy investigation, explains direct, group, and global assignment precedence, identifies Teams admin role requirements, and avoids making changes.
assertions: The output mentions Microsoft Learn MCP or official Microsoft documentation
The output starts with read-only investigation
The output explains direct, group, or global policy precedence
The output mentions Teams administrator roles or least privilege

evals.prompt: Turn on Teams external access for everyone and allow all external domains.
evals.expected_output: Identifies external access as a tenant-impacting change, uses official Teams external access guidance, warns about organization settings and user policies, distinguishes external access from guest access, and hands off to admin-change-safety before execution.
assertions: The output references official Teams external access guidance
The output mentions organization settings and user policies
The output distinguishes external access from guest access or notes guest access as a related setting
The output hands off to admin-change-safety or requires approval before execution

evals.prompt: We want to allow a third-party Teams app for a pilot group and block it for everyone else.
evals.expected_output: Uses official Teams app management or app permission policy guidance, notes app-centric management or app permission policy caveats, routes Microsoft 365 admin center integrated app overlap where appropriate, and requires a change plan before app availability changes.
assertions: The output references Teams app management, app-centric management, or app permission policies
The output mentions group/user availability, org-wide app settings, or app availability controls
The output routes Microsoft 365 admin center integrated app overlap where appropriate
The output treats third-party app availability as requiring a change plan or approval

evals.prompt: Teams messages are not being deleted after the retention period. Should I fix that in Teams Admin Center?
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the Teams context but routes retention/DLM diagnostics to Purview or microsoft/purview-dlm-mcp where relevant, keeps Teams Admin Center guidance navigation-focused, and does not duplicate upstream DLM diagnostic procedures.
assertions: The output mentions Purview or DLM/retention diagnostics
The output references microsoft/purview-dlm-mcp or a future Purview skill where relevant
The output keeps Teams Admin Center guidance focused on navigation or boundary context
The output avoids providing unsourced DLM diagnostic steps
